title: Introduce gated Terraform CI with live Conftest policy feedback loop
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Our current Terraform PR workflow runs a basic plan and terraform fmt but lacks early, developer-facing policy feedback and automated gating for unsafe changes to VPCs, IAM, or encryption settings. This leads to late security review cycles, rollbacks, and occasional manual coordination for upgrades and drift checks.

Goal: Implement a robust, opinionated Terraform CI pipeline for Private (VPC) stacks that provides immediate linting and policy-as-code feedback (Conftest/OPA), fails PRs with high-risk diffs, posts machine-readable plan comments to GitHub, and wires a short feedback loop so policy owners can iterate on Rego rules with minimal friction. The pipeline must be reusable across Terraform modules, support plan-only runs for PRs, and gated apply (manual/automated canary) for main branch merges.

Scope: - Pre-commit checks (terraform fmt, tflint) in local hooks and pipeline. - Plan generation in isolated workspace per PR, capture JSON plan output. - Conftest/OPA policy evaluation against plan.json with policy categories: network (subnets/egress), iam (privileged roles, wildcards), crypto (unencrypted S3/volume), resource quotas (unexpected GPU instances), mutable infra (destroy actions on prod resources). - Policy results posted back to PR as structured summary + rule links. - Failure severity mapping (blocker/allow-with-warning) configurable per repo via .policy-config. - Gate: Block merge if any blocker policy fails; allow warnings with an opt-in bypass in repo settings. - Drift detection job scheduled in staging and prod to detect unmanaged changes and open tickets. - Plan-approved artifact produced that can be used by a gated apply pipeline with audit trail.

Non-goals: Replacing external policy engines (Sentinel) or adding runtime runtime assert frameworks; we will integrate with existing SIEM later.

Why this approach: Conftest/OPA is lightweight, developer-friendly (rego is expressive), and already used in other infra teams. Posting machine-readable plan results shortens review cycles and reduces manual security triage. Gated apply gives us predictable rollouts for Private customers where infra changes have high blast radius.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline runs terraform fmt and tflint automatically for PRs and fails on formatting issues.
Terraform plan JSON is produced for every PR and evaluated by Conftest/OPA policies.
Policy failures are posted to the PR with rule id, severity, and actionable remediation guidance.
Blocking policy failures prevent merging to main; warnings are surfaced but do not block by default.
A plan artifact is produced for gated apply with a signed plan id and audit metadata (who triggered, git sha, timestamp).
Drift detector job runs daily in staging and weekly in prod and files issues for drift > threshold.
Documentation and onboarding doc available in Confluence and a small runbook for rollbacks/rollback playbook.
Automated tests exercise at least 8 representative policy scenarios (network, iam, crypto, destroy) in CI and pass.
Security review sign-off recorded in ticket and security_review_required flag set.
Monitoring: pipeline metrics (plan duration, policy failures, blocked PRs) are visible in Console dashboard.
Policy feedback loop documented: how to propose policy changes, test them locally, and ship updates with feature flag for new rule enforcement.
technical_notes: Use terraform 1.6.x in the pipeline container to ensure stable plan json semantics.
Plan generation: terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan && terraform show -json plan.tfplan > plan.json.
Conftest run: conftest test plan.json --no-color --output json. Store raw Conftest output as pipeline artifact.
Policy repo: github.com/redwood-inference/infra-policy-repo (branch: eng/ENG-274301). Policies must include metadata: id, severity, owner, test-cases.
PR comment format: header with severity counters, collapsed details per-failure, links to rule docs and reproduction steps, classifier tags for triage automation.
Gating: use branch protection + status checks to block merges on 'conftest/blocker' status. Warnings map to 'conftest/warning'.
Apply workflow: controlled by a separate pipeline that consumes a signed plan artifact and requires 2-step approval for production applies (operator + oncall).
Drift detection: use terraform plan in 'refresh-only' mode against state backend; threshold based on percentage changed resources to reduce noise.
RBAC: restrict who can update .policy-config and who can bypass blocker rules via CODEOWNERS and a policy-approver group in Okta/SAML.
Observability: emit metrics to telemetry endpoint for plan duration, conftest runtime, policy fail rate, blocked merges per repo.
test_plan: Unit tests: Conftest rule unit tests run in policy repo using mock plan.json fixtures. End-to-end: create ephemeral infra repo with representative changes, open PR, verify pipeline posts failures and blocks merge. Staging rollout: enable pipeline for a single private-vpc repo, observe two weeks of plan/drift metrics. Simulate a destructive change to validate block behavior and rollback path.
